answer: Each agent address must bond capital to a verifiable identity root, slashed on proof of duplicate control and locked through a long unbonding period. A Sybil operator funds every clone with the same bond, so faking the nth agent costs as much as the first. A rising tide of tiny wallets from one funding source is caught by graph analysis, and voting weight follows staked age, not address count, so a dune of fresh accounts earns near-zero share. A mirror check folds identities sharing a fingerprint or withdrawal address into one seat and burns the duplicate bond.
